note: How each order practises the path.

groups.where: Worldwide: Iraq, North and West Africa, South Asia, the Balkans
groups.self: A path of strict adherence to the Sharīʿa, sincerity and service.
beliefs: The law and the path are one.
Generosity, service and preaching to the public.

dhikr: Mainly aloud in gatherings, with silent dhikr too.
emphasis: Adherence to the law, sincerity, service, preaching.
shaykh: A guide to whom the seeker gives allegiance.
madhhab: Founder was Ḥanbalī/Shāfiʿī; followers of all schools.

groups.where: Iraq, Syria, Egypt, Turkey, the Balkans
groups.self: A path of humility and breaking the self.

shaykh: A guide to whom the seeker gives allegiance.

groups.note: Practices such as handling fire or piercing in some branches are criticised by many Sufis as well as others.

groups.origin: Abū al-Najīb al-Suhrawardī; Shihāb al-Dīn ʿUmar al-Suhrawardī (d. 632/1234), Baghdad
groups.where: Historically Iraq, Iran and India; today mostly within other orders
groups.self: A sober path tied to law, learning and order.
beliefs: Sufism as disciplined learning and manners.

shaykh: A guide to whom the seeker gives allegiance.

groups.origin: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Shādhilī (d. 656/1258), Tunis and Egypt; Ibn ʿAṭāʾ Allāh
groups.where: North Africa, Egypt, the Levant, worldwide branches (Darqāwī, ʿAlawī, Bāʿalawī links)
groups.self: A path of gratitude within ordinary life: no special dress, no leaving work.
beliefs: Gratitude over hardship as the way.
Remain in society and earn a living.

dhikr: Aloud in the ḥaḍra, with litanies (أحزاب).
emphasis: Gratitude, staying in society, no outward signs.
shaykh: A guide to whom the seeker gives allegiance.

groups.origin: Muʿīn al-Dīn Chishtī (d. 633/1236), Ajmer; Niẓām al-Dīn Awliyāʾ
groups.self: A path of love, serving the poor and staying away from rulers.
beliefs: Love and service of all people.
Independence from rulers and their gifts.

emphasis: Love, service to the poor, distance from rulers.
shaykh: A guide to whom the seeker gives allegiance.

groups.origin: Bahāʾ al-Dīn Naqshband (d. 791/1389), Bukhara; renewed by Aḥmad Sirhindī (Mujaddidī) and Khālid al-Baghdādī
groups.where: Central Asia, Turkey, the Caucasus, Kurdistan, South Asia, worldwide
groups.self: A sober path of following the Sunna and keeping inward presence with Allah.
beliefs: “Solitude in the crowd”: inward retreat while living among people.
Strict following of the Sunna, avoiding innovation.

emphasis: Sobriety, following the Sunna, inner awareness.
shaykh: Guide, with the heart’s bond to the shaykh (رابطة).

groups.self: A path received directly from the Prophet ﷺ, with simple fixed litanies.
beliefs: Litanies: ṣalāt al-fātiḥ, the waẓīfa, the hailala.
Exclusive affiliation: no other order alongside it.

silsila: Directly from the Prophet ﷺ, met awake (a claim others dispute).
shaykh: Exclusive: no other order may be joined.

groups.note: Claims about the founder’s direct meeting and the merit of ṣalāt al-fātiḥ are strongly disputed by other Sufis and non-Sufis.
